7ci7o7: The book club has a problem that at first seemed like good news: more participants arrive every month. The café where they used to meet no longer has enough tables and the noise makes it hard to hear those who speak softly. Some people propose moving to a municipal hall; others fear losing the informal atmosphere that made the group appealing.
1waonj1: In the forum, Laura wrote that she was glad about the growth, but that she was worried the solution would exclude those who get off work late. The municipal hall closes at eight. Iván defended the café because he knows the owners and believes they could reserve a quieter area. He doesn't know whether they would agree to do it every week. A third proposal is to alternate in-person meetings and online conversations, although several members don't have a quiet place to log in from.
8bw6e6: The coordinator asked each person to name one essential requirement and one preference. She then summarized the common points: they want to hear each other, arrive without rushing and keep costs low. There is no perfect option yet. So they agreed to try, for one month, a room belonging to an association that is open until nine. At the end of the trial they will ask who was able to take part and what difficulties came up. The final decision will depend on that experience, not just on who defended their idea with the most enthusiasm.
